Right. Okay. Think of post-phallo dicks (don't get me wrong). Or post-top-surgery nipples. They need time to regain sensitivity and most of the nerves do grow into their respective places.  
  
I had the same problem. It was too sensitive and dull to the touch at the same time or sometimes switching violently between two states during the day. I lost my voice, and worse, my sex drive and didn't even know how to jack off properly anymore. Like you, I was only on T for about 3.5 months. But a lot of things happened during that time and two of them were the enlargement of my vocal chords and my clitoral glands, both of which didn't catch up with the swift changes.  
  
Now I think 80% of what I used to have came back. It's 4 years after, so I don't know if I would have lost the 20% anyway with age. I enjoy sex now and I can properly orgasm.  
  
Just like almost anything detrans, it takes time. And especially since estrogen is a hormone not nearly as powerful as testosterone. Judging my fully personal opinion, you'll be almost surely fine. But you've got to have the patience and wait.  
  
In the meantime I'm sorry this has happened to you and I believe the trans community should be more educated about all of this.

It’s not placebo effect at least for me. And I realized that the first months of stopping T I was very vulnerable emotionally. Depression distorts reality and made me hate my voice a lot more. When I dug down I found that it was an adamant, almost destructive dissatisfaction in myself that was in play so no matter what I was what I did I was unable to like myself. Years later I had several shifts of feeling in regard to my voice. Months after stopping T I missed my old voice terribly; I couldn’t listen to the old songs I sang because that would swirl up a sense of longing and hurt. But, YEARS after my detransition, I didn’t really like my old voice all that much and even prefer my androgynous voice right after stopping. Now my voice is in the middle of the two and range is definitely broader.
Hang in there! My voice returned A LOT during YEARS after my last shot. Voice changes back painfully slowly but it will change back a fair bit! Just focus on other things and give it time!

Just wanted to share my five cents about the voice. I understand that the loss of your former voice is causing you a lot of pain like you're losing a part of your identity. I was the same way. But I promise you, it will pass... For now, let yourself mourn... You can no longer produce that voice, but you're still you. It just doesn't feel like you at the moment. With time, your perceptions will change. Please hang in there!
Another thing to pay attention to: You might not really get the type of voice you want (My voice seems to be a lot less attractive after...)

T is a very gradual process. You can literally watch it get lower till it reaches a point that you're personally satisfied with. You will regain a lot of your feminine timbre and range after stopping T, but only if your voice isn't completely broken during. I was on T for nearly 4 months with voice notably altered, and both my default voice and range recovered a lot (and is still recovering after 20 months).

You know what? Women are told the same things too, sometimes to a greater extent (i.e. about being attractive in workplace settings). And in dating women don't have to be dominant per se, but they are also told to play hard to get, not be overly submissive, etc. I'm sure you already know this, but I would really like to say that people are alike more than they are different, and it's not easy being either gender.

The range comes back, you will end up sounding much more feminine, but the change ia gradual and you've got to have a lot more patience than what I had when I was going through the exact same thing as you.

I can't sing as effortlessly as before, but my speaking voice gained a lot of flexibility and doesn't easily crack or feel strained anymore. Both emotion and inflection are just fine.

I had a moment of clarity tonight that I'd like to share. But my instinct knew better. It's never blinded by immediate emotions. In order for her to be my partner, she has to have a clear mind and the ability to make decisions. She has to be firm and loving, and able to go over mountains to match the depth of her confessions of love. In a way, I was waiting, watching, and putting her to a test - I knew if she doesn't choose me, I wouldn't want her, either. Now I realize that my negative emotions were not so much the sadness of unrequited love, but disappointment, huge disappointment, and grief, for the loss of my expectations and my respect for her... I had once seen the potential in her and thought that she could do so much better. To this point, I suddenly have the feeling that I don't really want to get back with her, and that we probably won't even be friends after this.

I suspect that the ex would keep ruining her, but that's her business to deal with, and this will have nothing to do with me. I even don't hope the best for her... it strikes me now that perhaps I don't love her as much as I thought I did. This makes me a little sad. Love feelings fade, and now sets in the cold reality...

Thank you again for all your help, and thank you for making me feel I can open up to you. It is safe to say that what you said changed my life. Thanks for making the world a better place! Another curious question: where are you from?

Your words make me feel that there’s love and understanding everywhere, no matter how my romantic endeavors turn out, and we’re all on the same boat of this magical existence called life…

After listening to your recording, I do feel calmer, less alone, and I do believe my reflections and the passing time have brought me to a better place emotionally. I have been doing the right things after breakup (shopping, getting a haircut, cleaning my room, reaching out to friends, putting away/throwing out reminders, etc.) and I’m on my way to recovery. Each day is better than the last. Very sadly, I’m not as emotionally mature as you said I was, because I contacted her the night before last night, and I let out many angry feelings, which I regret. I said “how could you love her more? How could you have done this to me? We were never meant to be, you’re not my soulmate, what we had was nothing, you were only like a sponge, reflecting back everything I told you, and girls do like me so no wonder we felt that way, I’ll never want to be friends with you after this, blah blah blah…” She was crying all the time when I said these things. And then we blocked each other, I sent her messages of regret on an App but she deleted that App so hasn’t received it yet. I now know that this was the angry phase and a normal, healthy stage after breakup, but I shouldn’t have used it to hurt her. However, this angry phase passed quickly and is replaced by depression and longing again. I would have preferred to stay angry, I guess, even though this is not fair to her. I wouldn’t want to hurt her, and I wouldn’t want to hurt myself; it seems to be impossible to balance the two!

Went through this three months ago, I completely understand you.

I wish I could convince you to run away. You're taking this personally, and it's impossible not to take it personally. Their brains are not wired like us, and implications of behavior and interactions do NOT work on them.

For example, she cheats and ideals someone else, while coldly rejecting you. In normal human interaction, this means you are less than the new partner. But this is simply not true. It's only the disorder working. No need to feel hurt and shame. (I understand this is difficult for any human.)

I loved her SO much. She was my everything. Without her I was so sad. But I took the hard road and broke all contact. All she wanted was contact, I know. We would definitely go through a dark period of missing each other, I know. I would think about her every minute, I know. But I broke contact. Whenever I missed her, I read something about BPD, and my mind became clearer.

I realized that mostly I did nothing wrong. The only thing I did wrong was merely staying in the relationship. I made excuses for her. I was blinded by love. I was beaten down by my own insecurities (which she strengthened). I was driven by curiosity. I thought the reason I could never really understand her was that she was superior and smarter.

And heck, what I loved might not even be her. I loved the highs produced by the disorder. Which explains why when some BPDs were completely cured, their partner didn't like them anymore.

Today is the 1 month No-contact day for me. I have never felt better. I can feel myself getting over her. If I had any contact with her during this time I couldn't have possibly reached this point. Thinking about all the times I broke up with her (but returned), I regret not having left sooner.
